$comment: What a network will let you do about an account, read from its capability values. Shared by tests/main/accounts.test.ts and the Android SharedCorpusTest. Both clients offer the same form, so both have to read the same answer out of the same string — a client that offers to register on a network that will not is offering a dead end.
$cases: `values` is the capability name to its value, exactly as CAP LS gave it. An absent capability is absent from the object; one advertised with no value is the empty string.

cases.name: rIRCd, which wants an email and a six-character password
registration with nothing said about it
no email needed, and only after connecting

cases.$comment: Most of IRC: SASL but no registration, so the account is made by talking to NickServ
cases.name: a network with services and no registration capability
a network with neither, where the password goes to NickServ as a message
case is not significant in a mechanism name

cases.$comment: A length nobody can satisfy is not a length. Reading it as zero would disable the check that exists to stop a refusal.
cases.name: a minimum that is not a number is no minimum
spaces around the values are ignored

cases.$comment: Libera's real list. It offers SHA-512 and not SHA-256, so a client that knew only the one fell back to PLAIN and sent the password to a server that never needed to see it.
cases.name: Libera, which offers SCRAM-SHA-512 and no SHA-256
a network offering both takes the stronger

$sharing: Whether both devices can be on this network at once. The precondition is always the same: both connections must authenticate to the same account, because the account is the only thing that makes the second one you rather than an impostor. A saved identify command is not enough — NickServ logs you in after registration, by which time the nick has already been refused.

sharing.name: SASL credentials, so both can arrive as the same account
a mechanism with no password gets nowhere
a password with no mechanism is never sent

sharing.$comment: The nick is refused during registration, and NickServ only answers afterwards
sharing.name: an identify command is too late to help
an empty mechanism is no mechanism

$views: Which half of the account screen to show. Their order matters more than any of them individually: a network that has not been reached cannot be asked what it can do, and somebody already logged in should not be offered a form to register the nick they are logged in as.

views.name: logged in and it will happen again by itself
never offer to register a nick you are logged in as
the network will make the account
and NickServ where it will not
